about: One ledger for the xMustard-owned process tree (PARITY_REQUIREMENTS §7, §12.4-12.5). Gate v2 (rss_bench_v2.py) attributes every sampled process to a component through process_roles; ledger_check fails a pull request whose measured delta against its base exceeds its workstream's line plus tolerance, grows any other owned component or the owned+external tree, or pushes a process past its §7.2 design line (the cumulative check); `rss_v2.sh ledger` reconciles the design lines, the §7.3 go_daemon items and the workstream lines and exits nonzero while a process is projected over its design line. CI judges a pull request by its base's ledger unless the budget-ledger-change label approves a change. A workstream's designated scenarios outside the CI suite block its pull request on the absolute 95.4 MiB gate only with gate_blocking: true: WS-30 and WS-55, whose acceptance names that gate there, and WS-13, since the overrun on agents-2-small is the per-agent stdio shims WS-13 removes; otherwise only on a regression (base median within the gate, head median over it). MiB = 2^20 bytes.

gate.metric: ps-RSS summed over the xMustard-owned tree in one snapshot every 100 ms; externals excluded and reported on their own lines

process_roles.about: Registered roots carry their own component. Descendants are matched by executable name (first matching rule wins; argv1 narrows a rule to a subcommand). Unknown descendants of owned processes count as owned (unclassified:<exe>). External rules and everything below them are never counted in the gate. owned_binaries are pulled in from agent trees: an xMustard binary an agent launched (hook client, shim, relay) counts toward the gate (§12.4 item on hook-client accounting).

go_daemon_suballocation.about: §7.3 targets inside the go_daemon design line (unmeasured). Each go_daemon workstream names the item its line lands in (workstreams[].item, WS-10's placement; owners may re-place). A base item's allocation is today's daemon, measured as the reference p50, so lines placed on it are compared at the process level only. Workstreams without an item are unallocated: §7.3 has no room for them.

reconciliation.about: The critic's §12.4 finding stands and is not decided here: the workstream lines overcommit the §7.2/§7.3 design lines. `rss_v2.sh ledger` prints the current numbers (at the 2026-09-25 reference: go_daemon 18.8 measured + 27.7 of lines = 46.5 projected against a 27 MiB design line; rust_index_service 37 of lines against 32; §7.3 governance caches 10.5 of lines against 3, evidence caches 6.5 against 2.5, hooks 1.5 against 1, runner 2 against 1, and 7 MiB of daemon lines with no §7.3 item; mcp_access 20.7 measured with the frozen workload's two stdio shims, and WS-13's -10 leaves 10.7 against a 0 line; rust_core_per_call 6.2 measured with only WS-25's -2 declared against a 0 steady line, although WS-02/WS-14 move per-call work into the resident service) and exits nonzero until the owner decides.
options: raise design lines: the gate cannot absorb the full 19.5 MiB go_daemon overcommit on top of the 87-93 MiB §7.2 peak
cut or re-place workstream lines so every process's lines fit its design line (for example SQLite-resident LSH bands and anchor postings per §12.4, WS-43 opt-in only)
declare offsetting savings as negative lines (§7.2 counts on -3 to -8 MiB from unlinking the platform half; only WS-49's -4 is declared)
reconciliation.enforced_meanwhile: ledger_check's design check fails any pull request whose measured process p50 on a CI-suite scenario is over its design line plus tolerance, and one that takes a process across that line on a designated scenario, so the overcommit fails CI when it materializes, whatever the lines say

tolerance.basis: Measured 2026-09-25 on darwin-arm64 (Apple M1, 8 GB, shared with other agents, load average 4-55). Tree peak: single v1-workload runs of one set of binaries ranged 66.8-87.9 MiB over 12 runs (the frozen v1's own history is 72.3-84.9 MB); medians of three were 74.2, 78.7 and 80.8 MiB, so CI compares medians of three and allows 10 MiB. Process check: go_daemon RSS p50 moved 17.8-23.2 MiB within one set of three (lazily reclaimed and compressed pages), footprint p50 11.0-13.1 MiB, so the check uses footprint p50 when both runs report it and allows 3 MiB. Between the medians of two sets of three runs of identical code, footprint p50 moved 2.0 MiB for go_daemon, 1.9 for rust_core_per_call and 4.0 for mcp_access (two stdio Go shims), hence 5 MiB for mcp_access. v1 cross-check: v2 minus the frozen v1 sampler in the same run stayed within 2.33 MiB in 19 of 20 runs and reached -5.62 MiB once at load average 25; it is a gross-error detector (a missed shim or core is 8+ MiB), so it allows 8 MiB. A line smaller than its check's tolerance is below measurement resolution (ledger_check reports BELOW_RESOLUTION, never PASS). Revisit all of these with CI-runner data.

reference_measurement.about: v1-workload (the frozen 501-file workload) measured by gate v2, median of three repeats. Binaries were built at source_head, whose api-go and rust-core trees equal feat/parity-v2 b4f7b49. The per-process p50 feeds the reconciliation's projected steady state and, for a process already over its design line here (mcp_access, rust_core_per_call, git_child), the cumulative bound ledger_check applies on this scenario: this p50 + the lines of the workstreams in merged_since (merged into the base after this measurement; none of the four listed is on such a process) + tolerance. Replace it with a CI-runner measurement when one exists, and clear merged_since then.
